text:
A: Alright, mate! Hiya! Last one, is it?
B: Hey! Yeah, I think so. Ollie. You okay?
A: Rhys. Yeah, I'm good, mate, good. Bit brain dead, I've been up since half four, so if I start talking rubbish, that's why, yeah?
B: Half four? That's brutal. What are you doing at half four?
A: Supermarket, stacking shelves. Early shift. You?
B: Student, geography at King's in London. And I do Saturdays in a running shop.
A: Running shop! So you're one of them running lads. I saw your trainers in the picture.
B: Guilty. Parkrun most Saturdays. I'm a bit obsessed, honestly.
A: I keep saying I'll start running. I say it every week. Then Wednesday comes, five-a-side, and I'm dead after ten minutes.
B: Wait, you do Wednesdays too? Same. Wednesday nights, mix of course mates.
A: No way. Are you any good?
B: We're alright. Not amazing. We lost five-one last week.
A: Five-one? We got battered seven-two! Half of us were still hanging from the weekend, to be fair. My mate Dai was in goal and he just sort of stood there watching it go past, like he was at a museum.
B: Ha! We had a guy do that. He said he was "reading the game".
A: Reading the game! Brilliant. Who do you support?
B: Watford. My dad's fault.
A: Cardiff. So we're both in pain, basically.
B: Pretty much. Do you do Fantasy Premier League?
A: I did, but I forgot to do my team for like six weeks and I was bottom of the league with the boys. They still bring it up.
B: That's the worst. I'm doing alright this year, but I've got a house league and the War Studies guy is beating me, which is unbearable.
A: War Studies? That's a thing?
B: Yeah, it's a whole course. He's lovely, he just never does the bins.
A: Ha! Sounds like me at home. My mam's always on about my room.
B: You still at home?
A: Yeah, with my mam and dad. Saving up, sort of. Not very well, like. I've been thinking about doing personal training, actually, maybe. You'd know about that, being into running and that. Is it worth it, do you reckon?
B: Erm, I know a couple of guys at the shop who've done it. I think the course is a few months, and then the hard bit is getting clients. But you're clearly good with people, so that's kind of half of it.
A: Aw, cheers, mate. Kind of half of it, yeah. I'll look into it. Now in a minute.
B: Now in a minute?
A: It's Welsh. Means soon. Or never.
B: Ha, I'm stealing that. That's my dissertation timeline.
A: Tidy. Do you go out much in London? Price of a pint there must be—
